Abstract title: Welcome/Intro/ housekeeping
name: Delia Boccia
description:
Delia Boccia is an internationally recognised expert in the social epidemiology of tuberculosis (TB) and in the role of social protection interventions in addressing health inequalities related to TB. Over the past five years, she has worked as a consultant for United Nations agencies, including the World Health Organization (WHO) and the World Food Programme (WFP), providing technical expertise to support the development, strengthening, and implementation of health and social protection policy agendas.
Prior to this, she spent more than a decade at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine, where she worked as a quantitative social epidemiologist. Throughout her academic career, she has conducted extensive research on the role of social protection in accelerating progress towards ending TB and reducing socioeconomic disparities in TB outcomes. Her research has contributed substantially to the evidence base underpinning Pillar 2 of the current WHO End TB Strategy.
Delia is currently based at the University of Turin, Italy, where she co-leads a work package within a large European Union Horizon project investigating the impact of social protection on the epidemiology and prevention of childhood and young-adult cancer across the EU. Her current work extends her longstanding expertise in social epidemiology and social protection to a broader range of health conditions and life-course outcomes.

description: Galyna Gorenko, MD, is a phthisiologist with extensive experience in tuberculosis (TB) prevention, diagnosis, and treatment in the Kirovohrad region of Ukraine. She serves as the General Director of the Kirovohrad Regional Phthisiopulmonology Medical Center and has deep expertise in managing drug-resistant TB, modern diagnostics, and patient-centered care models. Under her leadership, the region pioneered the use of artificial intelligence in radiology to detect TB. Her work focuses on strengthening medical infrastructure, integrating community-based services, and advancing innovative approaches to comprehensive TB control.

Abstract title: Perspective from Mongolia

description: Ganzorig Munkhjargal is Community Engagement and Advocacy Coordinator for the Mongolian Anti-TB Coalition. Since 2018, he has coordinated the STREAM CAB Mongolia, a vehicle for engaging affected communities in landmark clinical trials for drug-resistant TB. More recently, he joined the APCASO CAB to helm community engagement in TB research in Central Asia in partnership with the USAID-funded SMART4TB Project Consortium.

Abstract title: The ganfeborole development journey
name: Gareth Maher-Edwards
description: Gareth is a scientific director in Global Health Medicines at GSK and Medicine Development Leader for ganfeborole. With over 30 years in the pharmaceutical industry, spanning CROs, mid-sized, and large pharma. His expertise covers all stages of development, from candidate selection and translational medicine through to late-phase trials, regulatory submission, and post-marketing activities. He has worked across multiple therapeutic areas, including TB, CNS, rare diseases, gene therapy, and cardiovascular medicine. A strategic and innovative leader, Gareth is known for strong clinical development planning, effective global collaboration, and experience engaging with regulatory authorities including FDA and EMA.

Abstract title: From finding TB to preventing TB: how population wide active case finding could align with prevention and future vaccines
name: Gavin Churchyard
description: Dr. Gavin Churchyard is a physician scientist and President Emeritus of The Aurum Institute. He is an Honorary Professor at the University of Witwatersrand, and an adjunct Professor at Vanderbilt School of Medicine. He was a previous Chair of the ACTG TB Transformative Science Group overseeing a large programme of TB therapeutics research. He is the principal investigator on numerous large TB trials and has led and implemented numerous large cluster randomized trials. He has contributed to WHO guidelines for TB and HIV and has published widely in the areas of TB and HIV treatment and prevention.

Abstract title: Reimagining equitable tuberculosis (TB) policy for migrants with precarious status in Canada: implementation perspectives
name: Genevieve Armstrong
description: Genevieve Armstrong is an Assistant Professor and PhD candidate at the Lawrence Bloomberg Faculty of Nursing, University of Toronto. Her doctoral research examines how equitable tuberculosis (TB) policy and practice can improve access to diagnosis and treatment for migrants with precarious status in Canada. With a background in public health nursing and extensive experience in TB care, she has worked closely with migrant and Indigenous communities. Her work is driven by a commitment to health equity, social justice, and strengthening inclusive, community-informed approaches to TB policy and practice.

Abstract title: Accounting for migration in small area estimation of tuberculosis burden: Improving accuracy and reliability
name: Genevieve Dupuis
organization: Boston University School of Public Health
description:
Genevieve Dupuis is a PhD candidate in Biostatistics at Boston University's School of Public Health. In addition, she is currently a fellow in the FDA–ASA Oncology Educational Fellowship program.

Abstract title: Frontiers in relapse biomarker research

His research spans the divide between clinical and basic sciences in a high-TB-prevalence area.

Abstract title: Human genetic determinants of TB resistance and progression
name: Neel Gandhi
organization: Rollins School of Public Health and Emory School of Medicine
description:
Dr. Gandhi is a Professor in the Department of Epidemiology, with secondary appointments in the Departments of Global Health and Medicine (Infectious Diseases) at the Rollins School of Public Health and Emory School of Medicine. Dr. Gandhi has been engaged in clinical research in Tuberculosis and HIV since 1998. Dr. Gandhi leads a research team focused on epidemiology, clinical and translational research studies to improve care for TB patients and create new knowledge on the factors that influence transmission and susceptibility to TB, and the emergence of drug resistance. His research group is currently engaged in molecular epidemiology and geospatial studies to identify where and what factors impact the transmission of TB. They have projects examining the safety, pharmacokinetics and molecular mechanisms of new TB drugs (e.g., bedaquiline, delamanid). Further, his group is engaged in translational studies to understand immunologic, genetic and metabolomic factors that influence whether individuals become infected with TB, if exposed, and develop active TB disease, if infected. Dr. Gandhi’s studies are currently being conducted in South Africa, Ethiopia, Brazil and India.
 
In 2020, together with more than 25 colleagues across Emory University engaged in multidisciplinary TB-related activities, Dr. Gandhi helped establish the Emory Tuberculosis Center. The mission of the Emory Tuberculosis Center is to strengthen and expand expertise and opportunities for TB-related research, teaching and service at Emory and around the world. Dr. Gandhi serves at the Co-Director of the Emory Tuberculosis Center with Drs. Kenneth Castro and Jyothi Rengarajan.
